description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a drop in sustained throughput for a multi-part embeddings backfill starting 2026-03-09 23:00 UTC. Clients started seeing repeated 429 responses for long-running upload jobs despite apparent remaining tenant quota in the console. This manifested as 'soft' throttles — not a single sharp outage but a sustained elevated 429 rate that prevented the backfill from completing in normal time.

Impact:
- DataSift's nightly embeddings backfill (high-concurrency uploader) slowed by ~70%.
- Affects a production dedicated pool serving text-embedding-3-large; multiple parallel workers hit 429s across several hosts.
- Customer billing/usage reports looked normal; quotas in the console did not show full exhaustion.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-emb-01 (us-east-1)
- API path: POST /v1/embeddings/batch
- Client pattern: 80 concurrent worker processes per region, each streaming 8 concurrent chunk uploads (total ~640 parallel requests).

Steps to reproduce (observed in customer environment):
1) Start the backfill job with the same concurrency pattern described above.
2) Observe sustained 429s after 3–8 minutes.
3) Reduce concurrency to ~100 total active requests; 429s cease.

Observed behavior:
- 429 Intermittent responses across many worker hosts, with Retry-After headers present (~1–3s).
- Console token window shows non-exhausted but drifting refill behavior.
- Rate-limiter metrics show increased ingress from coordinator IPs counted against the tenant window.
- Autoscaler performed a scale-down event around the time the elevated 429s began.

Expected behavior:
- Coordinator-preflight requests and internal coordination traffic should be accounted against an internal/system bucket (or routed in a way that doesn't consume tenant tokens) so that client-initiated request tokens are the primary limiter.

Initial hypothesis:
- The distributed upload coordinator fanouts per-chunk preflight/validation requests (signed-url checks and small HEAD requests) which are being attributed to the customer's token window rather than internal agent traffic. During high fanout these preflight checks materially consume the tenant token window.
- A recent autoscaler scale-down caused worker churn: coordinator retried or re-fanned requests leading to duplicate preflight calls, amplifying token consumption.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Reduced client concurrency from 640 -> 100 total concurrent requests.
- Enabled a dedicated burst-pool option for this job (temporary policy change) which allowed the job to finish while we investigate.

Next steps (internal):
- Confirm rate-limiter attribution logic for requests originated by internal coordinators (ingress-proxy metadata headers).
- Reproduce locally with a small cluster and a mock coordinator that fans out HEAD/preflight calls.
- Add metric to distinguish 'preflight' calls vs user payload calls in token accounting dashboards.
- Engineering fix: tag internal probes with internal-agent header and route to internal bucket, or change accounting to ignore HEAD/signed-url preflight paths.
investigation_notes:
2026-03-10: Pulled rate-limiter traces for tenant account. Found sustained ingress from coordinator IPs (10.22.*) with high short-lived connections. Token-accumulator snapshot shows repeated small-charge events (~1–3 tokens each) aligning with preflight/HEAD timings.

2026-03-11: Replayed client pattern in staging with a mock coordinator; reproduced increased token burn and intermittent 429s when coordinator made preflight requests using the same customer API key. When coordinator used an internal agent token (test only) the tenant window remained stable.

Hypothesis validated: coordinator-originated preflight requests were being treated as tenant traffic. Autoscaler churn timing amplified retries and duplicated preflight checks which produced a steady drain.

Associated dashboards and logs:
- Grafana: dashboards/rate_limiter/tenant_window (spike correlation)
- Kibana: logs/proxy/tenant-247001 (request traces showing HEAD /signed-url-validation)
- Incidents: #support channel thread https://slack.redwood/support/thread/CF12345

resolution_notes:
(pending) Engineering PR prepared to ensure internal coordinator probes are routed to internal accounting bucket and to ignore HEAD signed-url validation from tenant token burn. Temporary mitigations: documented recommended concurrency limits for high-fanout upload coordinators and allowed burst-pool for this job.

Planned postmortem actions:
- Merge PR to rate-limiter and roll to canary (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/894).
- Add automated test to simulate coordinator fanout and assert token accounting.
- Update runbook: 'high-fanout-upload' with recommended safe concurrency and a checklist for enabling burst-pool.
- Notify Dedicated customers via release notes about improved internal probe accounting and suggested client patterns.
